scope: ELR-SEC-101 only: the internal trusted audit writer and its atomic integration with submitMatchSettlement and approveMatchScore.
scopeLimit: This is not an application-wide security or Android V1 release score. Moderation audit, server-side Claim, resumable account deletion, fan voting, disputes, player privacy separation, deployment, and device release gates remain open under ELR-SEC-102..104 and ELR-SEC-106..108 plus later waves.

target.verificationSource: Repository configuration, prior verified audit evidence, and local Firebase emulators. A live CLI database-list refresh timed out and no production mutation was attempted.

summary: The candidate tree has one non-callable, allowlisted audit writer. Match settlement and approval stage immutable audit events in the same Firestore transaction as their domain writes; malformed, unauthorized, failed, and idempotent retry paths cannot leave duplicate or partial audit state. No Firebase, Remote Config, Hosting, Android, or iOS deployment was performed.

evidence: functions/trusted_audit.js is an internal module and functions/index.js does not export an audit callable
the writer accepts only match plus matchScoreSubmitted or matchScoreApproved
actorId is supplied by authenticated operation cores rather than a client-selected audit payload
source is always trustedOperation and verificationVersion is always 1
beforePayload, afterPayload, and metadata are operation-curated and bounded by type, depth, key count, string length, and encoded size
the event ID is a deterministic SHA-256 fingerprint of entity type, entity ID, action, and operation request ID
submitMatchSettlement stages matchScoreSubmitted inside the settlement transaction
approveMatchScore stages matchScoreApproved inside the approval transaction with true pre-approval state
transaction create semantics prevent replacing an existing immutable event
failure injection proves an audit failure rolls back match, event, voting-session, standings, and audit writes
idempotent settlement and approval retries keep exactly one event per successful operation
unauthorized and invalid operations create no audit event
Firestore Rules deny direct client create, update, and delete for auditEvents
Rules emulator attacks pass for anonymous and authenticated direct-write attempts
Functions emulator smoke verifies real settlement and approval audit documents and retry behavior

attackMatrix.attack: authenticated client creates or edits an official audit event directly
client chooses an unknown entity type or action through the internal writer contract
operation supplies an oversized or unsupported nested audit payload
audit document creation fails after domain writes are staged
attackMatrix.expected: roll back the complete Firestore transaction

attackMatrix.attack: settlement or approval request is retried
attackMatrix.expected: one immutable event for the successful operation

attackMatrix.attack: unauthorized or invalid match operation is attempted
attackMatrix.expected: no domain write and no audit write

focusedFunctions.coverage: trusted writer, settlement, approval, entrypoint, idempotency, and failure injection

remainingRisks.risk: Fan voting and disputes still require trusted callables, atomic state transitions, and relationship-scoped reads.
Report and block operations do not yet use the trusted audit contract atomically.
Guest player and team Claim still run client-side and cannot yet produce trusted audit events.
Account deletion crosses Storage, Firestore, and Auth and still needs a resumable audited saga.
The full Android device regression from result approval through Pride sharing and Claim remains a release gate.

recommendations: Keep the audit writer internal and extend its action allowlist only inside the ticket that owns the corresponding trusted operation.
Do not copy free-form moderation details, phone numbers, claim tokens, relationship arrays, or full domain documents into audit payloads.
Publish the future Claim callable before locking the old client path, preserving SharePayload schema 1, pending login intent, and old shared links.
Run ELR-REL-504 on Android before release to prove settlement, approval, Pride Hub, sharing, and Claim still form one recoverable path.
releaseDecision: ELR-SEC-101 passes locally within its narrowed match-audit scope. Wave 1 and Android V1 remain open, and this audit authorizes no deployment.
